N233f705ccb12d4d8.open_question: Assess whether the permanent lease can bind the claimant mortgagee, distinguishing the parties, mortgages, dates, challenged and unchallenged prior findings, and open legal questions.

ORIGINAL_QUESTION.query: Assess whether the permanent lease can bind the claimant mortgagee, distinguishing the parties, mortgages, dates, challenged and unchallenged prior findings, and open legal questions.

T1c4a3b81c184c71b.SUPPORT: The core legal question is whether a mortgagor in possession had the power to grant a permanent lease before Section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act in 1929 to bind the mortgagee.
T1c4a3b81c184c71b.OPPOSITION: The defendants argue the lease is not binding because they were not parties to the mortgage suit and the auction sale could not end the lease.
T1c4a3b81c184c71b.EXCEPTION: The High Court applied Section 66, concluding the lease was valid because it did not render the Bank's security insufficient.

Tc0465f0d4cbe91b2.SUPPORT: The High Court held the lease valid under Section 66 because the security was not rendered insufficient, despite no specific allegation in the plaint.
Tc0465f0d4cbe91b2.OPPOSITION: The Privy Council must determine if the mortgagor had the power to grant the lease under the law existing at the time of the 1925 grant.
Tc0465f0d4cbe91b2.EXCEPTION: The trial court found the plaintiff subrogated to the Bank's position and the defendants bound by the mortgage decree, but the High Court negatived constructive res judicata.

Tb6cbe9b73d77f4df.SUPPORT: The trial court found the plaintiff subrogated to the Bank's position and the defendants bound by the mortgage decree, but the High Court negatived constructive res judicata.
Tb6cbe9b73d77f4df.OPPOSITION: The defendants argued the decree was not binding as they were not parties to the mortgage suit.
Tb6cbe9b73d77f4df.EXCEPTION: The High Court considered the power to lease under Section 66, finding the security was not rendered insufficient.

T972ace70bb20383b.SUPPORT: The defendants contended the decree was not binding as they were not parties to the suit and the Patta could not be ended by the auction sale.
T972ace70bb20383b.OPPOSITION: The plaintiff contended he was subrogated to the Bank's position and the decree was binding the defendants.
T972ace70bb20383b.EXCEPTION: The trial court held the plaintiff was subrogated and the defendants were fully represented in the mortgage suit.

Tdfe00f08a81a1818.SUPPORT: The provided text ends before the Privy Council's judgment, leaving the ultimate resolution of the legal question open.
Tdfe00f08a81a1818.OPPOSITION: The High Court dismissed the plaintiff's suit, holding the lease valid and not affected by the mortgage or execution sale.
Tdfe00f08a81a1818.EXCEPTION: The Privy Council admitted the appeal on 9th January, 1946, to consider the power to grant the lease.
